title: Introduce tenant-scoped operator allowlist and epoched append-only audit lock
author: Daniel Ortega
ci_status: pass (one flaky test fixed after rerun)
description:
Context: This change implements a tenant-scoped operator allowlist and an epoched append-only audit lock to improve compliance guarantees when operator-scoped credentials are used with region/KMS constraints. Motivation: customers in regulated environments asked for stricter guarantees that operator-initiated actions are scoped to tenant-allowlisted operators and that audit records for those actions are immutable within a time epoch to prevent accidental rewrites during bulk reingestion or migration.

What this PR does (single-line description + what to expect):
- Add a tenant-scoped operator allowlist that gates operator tokens by (tenant_id, operator_fingerprint, region_hint). This is enforced at the policy-evaluation boundary and in the operator-auth middleware.
- Introduce an "audit epoch lock": a lightweight append-only marker for tenant audit streams that prevents in-place edits for events assigned to a closed epoch. Epochs are short-lived (configurable per-tenant) and allow safe bulk replays without risking historical mutation.
- Wire KMS-origin verification into the operator allowlist checker: operator entries carry an optional KMS binding (kms_provider:kms_keyid) checked at run-time for service accounts that delegate wrapping keys.
- Migration tooling and docs: an examples/migrations/README and a db migration script to add operator_allowlist and audit_epoch tables.

Why this approach: The allowlist gives an explicit, compact representation of allowed operator bindings and makes it simple to reason about cross-region operator delegation. The epoch model is intentionally append-only and not a full WORM store; it prevents accidental in-place modification while keeping operational recovery straightforward.

Compatibility and rollout plan:
1) Feature is behind feature flags: rbac.allowlist.enabled and audit.epoch_lock.enabled. Flags default to off.
2) Backwards compatible reads: services that do not opt in will continue to use current policy flow.
3) We recommend a staged rollout: enable allowlist enforcement in shadow/dry-run mode for 7 days, reconcile denylist hits, then flip enforcement; enable epoch lock in audit-ingesters first (regionally) and monitor ingestion latencies for 72 hours.

Checklist:
- [x] Core allowlist implementation (policy + middleware)
- [x] Audit epoch lock write-path and sanity-checks
- [x] Migration script and example SQL
- [x] Unit and integration tests for typical and edge cases
- [x] Docs and runbook additions (operator-affinity.md, migrations README)
- [x] KMS-origin verification for allowlist entries

Notes on security review: This PR integrates with the KMS client to surface key origin data. We intentionally do not modify KMS key permissions; we only assert provider:key metadata presented by the KMS client. Operators without a KMS binding still work but must be explicitly allowlisted.

Release notes (short): Introduces tenant-scoped operator allowlist and epoched audit-locks to improve audit immutability and operator scoping controls. Opt-in via feature flags. See docs/operator-affinity.md for migration steps.

Related: ENG-3421 implements the backend schema; SEC-178 tracked the compliance ask; SUP-4021 is a support case that motivated the runbook additions.

review_comments: Maya Chen (2025-11-04): Can we ensure the allowlist lookup has an LRU-backed cache with TTL to avoid a DB hit on every auth check? Suggested adding metrics for cache hit/miss. Response: added a small in-memory cache with configurable TTL and metrics in allowlist.go (see commit 6e2d89f).

Ethan Ruiz (2025-11-06): The audit epoch lock write path needs an idempotency token to tolerate duplicate deliveries from the ingest path. Also asked for more aggressive testing around partial epoch closure. Response: added idempotency checks and added an integration test for double-post idempotency (tests/integration/tenant_affinity_test.go).

Priya Nambiar (2025-11-07): Security review - please clarify KMS-origin trust boundary and what to do if KMS provider metadata is absent. Response: clarified in docs and code: if KMS metadata is absent we only allow operator entries that do not require a KMS binding; enforcement mode can block non-bound operators per-tenant policy. We also added a feature flag to disable KMS-origin enforcement globally.
Maya Chen (2025-11-10): Approved after minor nits fixed in docs and a test flake addressed (CI rerun passed).

release_notes:
- Feature: tenant-scoped operator allowlist (opt-in behind rbac.allowlist.enabled)
- Feature: epoched append-only audit locks to protect historical audit immutability (opt-in behind audit.epoch_lock.enabled)
- Migration: new DB tables operator_allowlist, audit_epoch; see migrations/20251103_add_operator_allowlist.sql and docs/operator-affinity.md for steps.
operational_runbook: Added a runbook section in docs/operator-affinity.md covering shadow mode rollout, reconciling denylist hits, and rollback steps for audit epoch lock. Key steps: enable shadow mode, monitor allowlist hits metric, follow migration order: DB migration -> enable shadow allowlist -> reconcile hits -> flip enforcement. If ingestion latency spikes after epoch lock, disable audit.epoch_lock.enabled per-region and re-run ingest in backlog mode.
notes: This is intentionally conservative: enforcement is opt-in and migration steps are additive. We validated that audit ingestion tail is unaffected in disabled mode. Tests exercise KMS-origin absent/present permutations.
